truths.truth: Run with v123456789012345678901.0.0 or v18446744073709551616.0.0, the signer exits non-zero, prints exactly the usage line on stderr under /bin/sh and dash, and calls neither gh nor ssh-keygen; a test signs nothing for such a version (ROADMAP SC1, SC3; AC1)
truths.evidence: crates/terminus/tests/sign_release.rs:434-456 adds both tags to a_bad_tag_is_refused, which asserts non-zero exit, stderr exactly 'terminus: usage: sh scripts/sign-release.sh v<X.Y.Z>\n', and empty gh and ssh-keygen logs. The single full-suite run (cargo test --workspace --all-features, exit 0) shows a_bad_tag_is_refused::sh ... ok and a_bad_tag_is_refused::dash ... ok. Spot-check in a scratch folder with the real install.sh and logging stand-ins for gh and ssh-keygen: the new signer under sh and dash gives rc=1, stderr 'terminus: usage: sh scripts/sign-release.sh v<X.Y.Z>', and no log file for both tags. The same run with main's signer (git show main:scripts/sign-release.sh) reaches 'gh release view v18446744073709551616.0.0 ...' and 'gh release view v123456789012345678901.0.0 ...', so the test fails against the old copy and pins the bound.

truths.evidence: grep -c -E '^[[:space:]]*valid_version[[:space:]]*\(' scripts/sign-release.sh prints 0. git diff main..HEAD -- scripts/sign-release.sh deletes the old valid_version() ( ... ) block (the copy with no 20-digit or u64 bound). The only remaining mentions are the cut loop's string compare at :63, the fail message at :52 and :67, the count regex at :51, and the call at :69.

truths.truth: Beside an install.sh with no valid_version, two, or an unclosed one, the signer exits non-zero with one stderr line naming install.sh and calls neither gh nor ssh-keygen (AC4)
truths.evidence: No permanent test (PLAN Notes say so on purpose); settled by the PLAN Task 1 hand check, run in the scratchpad with env -i PATH=<stand-ins>:/usr/bin:/bin under sh and dash. (a) function removed: rc=1, 1 stderr line 'terminus: scripts/../install.sh: needs exactly one valid_version function, found 0', no log. (b) function doubled: rc=1, '... found 2', no log. (c) cut off after the definition line: rc=1, 'terminus: scripts/../install.sh: needs a valid_version() ( line and a ) line closing it', no log. Extra case (d), a second definition in another form ('  valid_version () {'): rc=1, '... found 2', no log. All 8 runs give the same result under sh and dash. Code: scripts/sign-release.sh:51-52 and :67.

truths.evidence: git diff --quiet main -- install.sh exits 0 (working tree) and git diff --quiet main HEAD -- install.sh exits 0; git diff --stat main..HEAD lists no install.sh. The one full-suite run of cargo test --workspace --all-features exits 0: 992 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored, including all 17 sign_release tests. sh -n and dash -n on scripts/sign-release.sh both exit 0.

truths.truth: The check the signer runs is install.sh's own valid_version, every line of it, cut out at run time and run on the tag's version before the first gh call (ROADMAP SC2; goal)
truths.evidence: Running the signer's own cut loop (scripts/sign-release.sh:53-66, taken verbatim) on the repo's install.sh under sh and dash produces text that cmp reports identical to install.sh:58-77, all 20 lines including the 20-digit and u64 checks. scripts/sign-release.sh:68 evals it and :69 calls valid_version "$version" || fail "$usage", before the first gh call at :73. One value traced end to end: tag v18446744073709551616.0.0 enters as $1 (:34), becomes version (:36), is refused by the cut function at :69 with the usage line and never reaches gh (truth 1 spot-check); v18446744073709551615.0.0 takes the same path and lands in 'gh release view' (truth 2 spot-check). The test fixture writes the shipped install.sh with only the key swapped (sign_release.rs:189-205), so every test runs the real function.
